utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Zyrapi, the other Defence counsel will now cross-examine -- yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've had an opportunity to discuss the position amongst ourselves, in light of Your Honour's suggestion at the end of the day, and with the acquiescence of all Defence counsel and subject to the limits that Your Honour indicated yesterday, it has been agreed - again, of course, subject to Your Honour's approval - that I should complete the last two topics of cross-examination that I had planned to deal with, and that will leave sufficient time for the other two counsel to complete their cross-examination within the first session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Consent is there. That means, Mr. Zyrapi, that Mr. Emmerson will put a few more questions to you, and then other Defence counsel for the accused will cross-examine you. In answering these questions, you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, as you gave it at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, in the November 2005 statement, in paragraphs 43 to 45, and again in the April 2007 statement paragraph 45, you refer to an incident that took place in late August or early September in which you, together with a delegation from the General Staff, visited the Dukagjini area to intervene in what you described as a dispute with FARK, with Tahir Zemaj, the commander of the forces of FARK, F-A-R-K, and the position is summarized by the Prosecution in a summary that was read at the beginning of your testimony, on the basis that the KLA General Staff sided with Ramush Haradinaj in this dispute. I just want to ask you some further questions about that aspect of your evidence and to assist the Trial Chamber a little, if you can, please, with the political background to the position with FARK and KLA. You told us yesterday, Mr. Zyrapi, that the individuals who described themselves as the General Staff had, you believed, been appointed by the LPK, that is the Popular Movement of the Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that there was, in effect, a political organisation linked to those General Staff individuals. Is that -- is that the position?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And again, so the Judges understand, there was an entirely separate political organisation in operation at the time known as the Democratic League for Kosovo, the LDK. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Democratic League of Kosova existed even in the past and operated as a political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the formal president of the LDK was Ibrahim Rugova. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you confirm, please, that during the 1990s, there was a split within the LDK between those like Rugova, who were promoting a non-military solution to the conflict with Serbia, and a separate faction under the command of Bujar Bukoshi, who were advocating armed struggle within the -- within the parameters of the LDK?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was in the 1990s because I wasn't there, but with respect to the -- to Bujar Bukoshi, he was prime minister of the exile government in the diaspora.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that was what I was going to come to. A government in exile was set up outside Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Bujar Bukoshi was the prime minister or so described of that government. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And an individual called Ahmet Krasniqi was described as the minister of defence. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, did this government have a democratic mandate or was it simply a group of individuals who called themselves a government?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was formed in exile. I don't know when exactly because I wasn't there, but it was elected by the vote.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A vote within Kosovo, of people within Kosovo, or a vote of a group of individuals who wanted to form a government? How did it -- how did it come about, as far as you understand, the position?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you explanation for that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because I wasn't there present.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. But you can confirm that Bujar Bukoshi was in favour of armed intervention in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And are you aware of the existence of a completely separate fund from the homeland calling fund which you've described, a separate fund known as the 3 per cent fund which was used by Bukoshi and the LDK to form a military organisation?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 3 per cent fund existed at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, just so that the Judges understand, you have a General Staff of the KLA operating in Tirana; and then a separate military and political structure under the LDK. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you aware that in the second half of June, the LDK sent a contingent of soldiers under the name of FARK into Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember, it was a group which entered with Tahir Zemaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so. And, again, roughly speaking, 120 soldiers with 25 trained officers?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but I do know that it was a group that came.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, by that time, by -- I'm going to put a date of the 24th of June to you, by the 24th of June, you were in an operational position, you've told us, within the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 24th of June, I was in the operational department but not its leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I understand that. I understand you weren't its leader -- its leader. But it was your function to go around on the ground and assess forces, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you informed in advance that this group were coming into Kosovo at that time before they arrived?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So despite having the responsibility that you did have, nobody had told you that there was a group of 120 officers of the separate political organisation who were going to enter into the Dukagjini region?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I take it that "officers" is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: 120 officers and 25 soldiers. Let me put the question again. Despite the fact that it was your function to assess military capability on the ground within Kosovo, nobody had informed you that there was a contingent of FARK soldiers about to enter the Dukagjin region?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not informed. Then I was informed when they came.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know if the General Staff were aware that they were going to come at that time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so it would follow, presumably, that none of the commanders on the ground would have known that this contingent was coming?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want then, against that background, please, to ask you to turn to tab 9 in the yellow bundle -- I do apologise, tab 8, first of all --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which is, for the record, marked for identification as Exhibit P199.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and just ask you to confirm, please, that that is an order signed by Ramush Haradinaj appointing Tahir Zemaj as commander of the 1st Brigade command on the 12th of July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that appointment had obviously been made before you arrived in the Dukagjini area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware that Ramush Haradinaj had made arrangements for these FARK officers to be positioned at the barracks or a large building in Prapaqan?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was informed that they were stationed in the school of Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you visit that school?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the middle of July, when you visited in mid-July?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember to have been in July, but I do know that I went there for the second time when I went there in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Thank you. Now, these soldiers had been formally incorporated within the KLA in Dukagjin, had they not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But there was a difficulty of which you were aware, I think; namely, that because they believed themselves to be operating under the authority of the government in exile, Tahir Zemaj was reluctant to spread the officers around to the different parts of the Dukagjin region where they were needed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He wanted to keep all his 25 militarily trained officers together, rather than sharing them around in the units where they would be most effective. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: From your point of view, in terms of military effectiveness, it would -- would you agree that it would have been far preferable for the KLA's fighting capability if officers with military experience had been dispersed to the areas of conflict rather than leaving untrained villagers with guns in the absence of a proper -- properly trained military personnel?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But the problem was that Tahir Zemaj was taking orders from somebody else outside Kosovo. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could just turn behind tab 9 for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could we just try to find out what actually the basis of the knowledge of the witness is in this respect. Could you tell us, if you say from what you remember, Tahir Zemaj was taking orders from someone else outside Kosovo, how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We're just about to, I think, move to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I put a question to the witness. Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. On the basis of information I received and when I visited the Dukagjin Zone, the commander told me this, as well as from the members of the staff who were informed that he was receiving orders from outside Kosova; namely, from the government in exile and the late minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think that that formed part of the discussion that took place when you went there at the end of August/beginning of September to resolve the problem that had arisen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we can just turn behind tab 9 for a moment, please. This is a document dated the 21st of August, and again, if I can just summarize it and ask you to agree with it. This document records that on the 21st of August, the command for the Dukagjin Plain was re-organised with Tahir Zemaj becoming the overall commander of the operational staff of the plain of Dukagjin, and Ramush Haradinaj being subordinated to the position of deputy commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from what I see here, and this is what I was informed of.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this was the issue that brought you to the Dukagjin region at the end of August/beginning of September, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, that's Exhibit P252 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, just pausing there for a moment, you were aware, were you -- perhaps I can put the question a different way. Were you aware of the reasons why Ramush Haradinaj had yielded the overall command to Tahir Zemaj on the 21st of August? Do you know why it happened?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, after we received the information that this was the case, in talks I had with Ramush, Ramush thought that this was the order or the belief of the General Staff, that is, for this change to occur, since we didn't make any decision in the General Staff that this change take place in the Dukagjin Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So Ramush told you when you arrived, he had believed it was the will of the General Staff that Tahir Zemaj should take over from him; is that -- is that the position?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that he believed that the order came from the General Staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- for this change to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You knew, though, didn't you, that during the first couple of weeks of August, there had been a major Serb offensive in the area of Gllogjan, and that Ramush Haradinaj and his forces had been forced out of Gllogjan and thoroughly beaten militarily at that point?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This happened even earlier in Reka e Keqe zone, and that fell under the control of the Serbian forces as a result of their attacks. These attacks started not only in Dukagjin but also in other areas --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But -- I understand that. But specifically in Dukagjin, the heartland of Ramush Haradinaj's control in Gllogjan was overrun and fell to the Serbs on about the 12th of August, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned of this when we arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And did you also learn that it was as a result of him being militarily defeated at that point, that Tahir Zemaj had been elected to take over as zone commander?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the conversations we had, this was one of the reasons presented. But at that time Tahir Zemaj had received orders to make that change, to take over the command, to prove that he had the capability to lead and continue to be the commander of the Dukagjini Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And who had he received those orders from specifically?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I talked with this -- about this problem, I was told that he had received orders from the minister of defence of the government in exile.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the alternative political military structure to your own?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've seen this minute before. It's plain, is it not, that Ramush Haradinaj consented to yield control at that point?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived there, that had been done. So he was deputy commander and obeyed all the orders of the then-commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And then I think you arrived on about the 1st of September. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain whether it was the 1st of September or the 3rd of September. I know that it was the end of August and the beginning of September when we arrived in Dukagjin Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it was yourself, Rexhep Selimi, and Hashim Thaqi who arrived in the area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was me, Hashim Thaqi, Rexhep Selimi, Lahi Brahimaj, and some others, but I don't remember exactly who.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the purpose of your visit was to challenge the decision that had been taken and to remove Tahir Zemaj. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went there to discuss this issue and to replace the zone commander since we didn't make any decision for the change that had occurred and for Ramush Haradinaj to continue to be the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think, though, you've described it at various points as being a visit to intervene in a dispute, but I think you've just agreed, have you not, that by the time you arrived, Ramush Haradinaj was perfectly content to operate as deputy zone commander, working to Tahir Zemaj?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was operating in that capacity, and when I talked with him, he said, I will obey any orders coming to me from the staff. But the staff had made a decision to reinstate him to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, the dispute was between the LPK members of the General Staff and the LDK, who were giving orders to Tahir Zemaj. The dispute was between the group that you were with and those who were giving Tahir Zemaj his orders. It was, effectively, a power struggle between those two groups, wasn't it, rather than between the two commanders?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- as you say, it was a power struggle, not a struggle between two individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your group wanted to have a commander on the ground that controlled the Dukagjin area as part of the KLA, and the government in exile wanted to have their commander controlling the Dukagjin region. That's basically what was happening, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the problem in essence, but also that the commander of a zone could not be replaced while he was acting as commander and doing his duties in the area. Changing commanders at that moment in time was something that was very wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But of course, Tahir Zemaj believed he had the authority of the so-called government in exile, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was there a -- during this visit, a direct telephone conversation between Hashim Thaqi, for your side, and Ahmet Krasniqi, the minister of defence of this government in exile? Was there a direct contact between the two?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes, there was a telephone conversation, but I don't know what they talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Essentially, they were having a row, weren't they, about who was in charge and who had legitimacy?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, it was a power struggle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, your first answer was that you didn't know what they were talking about, and then Mr. Emmerson asked you: "Essentially, they were having a row, weren't they?" And then you said: "Of course, it was a power struggle." Now, did you hear the content or part of the content of the conversation, or is this an inference and conclusion you've drawn from that situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not hear the conversation because I was not close to the person who was conducting the conversation. This is just my assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please be very careful in telling us exactly what are assumptions and what is your knowledge of the facts. And, Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- would you please take care that if a witness says, I didn't hear what they said, and then you tell him what it most likely would have been, that you're more or less soliciting assumptions which would not assist the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I can just ask one further question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you discuss with Hashim Thaqi what had taken place after he came off the telephone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because there were operations going on in the area of Dukagjin. There were other things we had in our minds, so we didn't discuss this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But in the end a decision was taken, was it not, by those present to reverse the change that had been made on the 21st of August. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we just look behind tab 11, which is Exhibit P259 marked for identification, the then-commander Tahir Zemaj issued on the 3rd of September an information to all local staffs referring to a meeting of some persons from the KLA General Staff on the 2nd of September which had rejected the earlier decision. And he, therefore, informed local staffs that the previous command structure would be put back in place, that is to say with Ramush as the overall commander, Ramush Haradinaj as the overall commander, but with Tahir Zemaj as deputy zone commander. Is that -- is that the position?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We issued the order to reinstate Ramush Haradinaj to the post of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had not seen this document before. This is the first time I'm laying eyes on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Two final questions, if I may, and very briefly. In the statement you made and the evidence that you gave in the Limaj case, you referred to a document called "The Provisional Regulations For the Organisation of the Army's Internal Life." Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There seems to be -- there seems to be some confusion about when it was produced. Can I ask you to confirm the evidence that you gave in the Milutinovic case, that that document was first produced at the end of 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The regulation of the General Staff existed earlier, but in 1998 it was completed and expanded, as far as I remember, but it did exist as a rule book before.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, Mr. Zyrapi, do be careful with your evidence on this. The document I am referring to is the document: "Provisional Regulations For the Organisation of the Army's Internal Life." Now, you gave evidence in the Milutinovic case, page 5945, line 15, that that document was prepared at the end of 1998, and that it was a first draft at that stage?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now I remember this document. This was a provisional document that organised the life of the army, yes, and it was compiled by the end of 1998, and then it was sent to the units on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that was after you became Chief of Staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally this: There is reference in one of your statements, November 2005, paragraph 37, to reports of people being killed who were suspected collaborators. I'd like to ask you to confirm, please, that you are not aware of any specific instance involving the killing of suspected collaborators in the Dukagjin region in the summer of 1998, that is to say up until the end of September 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement that I gave in November, I have explained clearly that I heard through the media and the communiques about such things, but I never saw, myself, any such case. As regards the Dukagjin Zone, I never heard of any such cases while I visited, and I did not see anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith, I'd like to put one clarifying question to the witness in relation to his last answer. You said you have explained clearly that you heard through the media about such things, and then you said but you never saw any such case. And as regards the Dukagjin Zone, you never heard of any such case while you visited. Could you tell us some specifics about some of these cases in the other zones, not in the Dukagjin Zone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said earlier and as I've explained in my statement, I heard about such cases, but even when I visited other zones I didn't see any myself, I mean, any cases of killings. It's just something I heard through the media mainly. But keeping in mind that I was on the move all the time and the time restrictions I have -- I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were the media specific about what had happened where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, no, there were no details. The electronic media and the Albanian satellite television presented such cases, such instances. I was following -- trying to follow the media at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, what makes you believe that this happened in other zones but not in the Dukagjin Zone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because the media mentioned names of places or territories where this had allegedly happened, but, as I said, in the areas I visited, I never encountered such instances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I do understand. But did the media never refer to any event or any place which would be within the Dukagjin Zone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't remember, and even during my visits and my tours, I don't remember ever hearing such a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Guy-Smith. You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to return for a moment to your -- your time in Tirana when, I believe, you told us that you were living in an apartment with Naim Maloku. Apart from yourself and Naim Maloku, was anybody else living in that apartment?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I said earlier that it was me, Naim, Agim Cela, Afrim Basha, as far as I remember, and several others.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And -- and would it be fair to say that the apartment that you were living in was one of the weigh stations or stopping places for people to come who were interested in volunteering to fight in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This apartment was a waiting station maybe for me and a couple of others but not in general. It was not considered as a basis for other people to stop there before they went to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time, you were living in Tirana with Naim Maloku and Afrim Basha. Do you recall meeting Naim Hazeri, Bekim Shyti, or Mensur Kosumi at the apartment?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mensur Kosumi was a member of the group that I was part of. This Mr. Shyti, I think I've seen him but not in the apartment. He was a member of one of the groups that was trained in Albania at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if I understand your testimony correctly, you do not remember meeting Idriz Balaj at the apartment in Tirana, but he told you when you met him in Irzniq that the two of you had met in Tirana. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also said this in my statement that it is possible that we met because many people followed that route, and I've met so many people in Tirana that I don't remember all of them. But it is possible that we met.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The first time that you do recall meeting Idriz Balaj was in Irzniq on your July visit; right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I remember that I saw him for the first time -- or to my recollection, I saw him for the first time when I went to Dukagjin in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that was a day when you also met a gentleman who I believe his name is Shemsedin Qeku, who was another commander in Irzniq. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, you had an opportunity to speak with Shemsedin Qeku in your capacity as being involved in the operational department in attempting to assess the forces that were involved in the area; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I met Shemsedin and we talked about those issues, but it was a very brief meeting, and I considered him a colleague because he also was a former officer in the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He was somebody who you had -- you had actually worked with before, isn't that correct, when you were both in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not work together with him in the same unit, but both of us served in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Now, after you spoke with -- with Mr. Qeku, you learned that Idriz Balaj was involved with a rapid intervention unit; right? That's what you've told us and that's, in fact, what happened?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, as far as I remember at that time was -- when I was touring, I also visited Idriz Balaj and the rapid intervention unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: While you were with Idriz Balaj and you were talking with him, you learned, among other things, learned that he was called Toger or Togeri; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but also the zone commander told me this earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you also learn during the time that you were speaking with him about the efforts that the unit had engaged in, in such places as Voksh, Sllup, Drenovac, when they were fighting and had operated as a front line rapid intervention unit?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether we talked about this. As I said, I was there for a very brief period of time. It could have been that they mentioned such a thing, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What you did learn when you were introduced to him is that his efforts were such that he was considered by at least Ramush and I also believe, if I'm not mistaken, Mr. Qeku to be a brave and courageous man who was willing to fight for the freedom of his country. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When Ramush introduced him to me, he said that he is the leader of the rapid intervention group or unit, and that he had experience, he had taken part in the war in Croatia, and he was a brave person.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you -- did you have a chance to speak with -- with Toger concerning the type of training that he was giving to the -- to the soldiers who were fighting in his particular unit, so you could assess how best they might be deployed and could give some advice in that regard?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember all the details of the conversations we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you tell us whether you made a determination precisely what kind of weaponry that unit had?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I just remember that the unit had been formed, it was there, and they had some weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you -- did you learn in your conversations with your former colleague, Commander Qeku, what the relationship was between Commander Qeku and Toger in terms of how matters were to be attended, specifically in Irzniq and in the surrounding areas?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember ever speaking about this with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During your time in Kosovo, did you hear of a gentleman by the name of Fadil Nimani?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, if you haven't -- when you say you don't remember the name, if I were to suggest to you that Fadil Nimani was the gentleman who was responsible for forming the rapid intervention unit in the Dukagjin Zone, would that be of assistance in you remembering the name?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Apart from the -- the one time that you had occasion to -- to meet, which I -- I gather was for, as you've told us, a very brief period of time in your visit to Irzniq, did you have a chance to ever liaise with Toger again and -- and discuss military matters with regard to how to deploy units or where best to -- to focus efforts in terms of the fights?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember speaking to him again. I talked to him when I was in -- there in July. I don't remember seeing him in August when I went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I went short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Start out with apologising twice. I've got a terrible cold, and I will try not to be too indistinct to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I represent Lahi Brahimaj, with whom you worked as a member of the General Staff in central Kosovo in the summer of 1998. I'd like to ask you a few points in relation to the testimony you've given so far. As I understand it, you say in mid-July you visited Dukagjin as part of your responsibility for evaluating KLA positions, strengths, and weaknesses in general. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went there in mid-July 1998, I went there because there was also a meeting of the General Staff with Dukagjin Operational Zone, but also to get acquainted with the units and the positions and what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, it may be that there is a slight difference of recollection between yourself and Mr. Brahimaj; it may be that this isn't terribly important, but I'd like to suggest, sir, for your consideration that there was not a General Staff meeting in the Dukagjin Zone at that stage, and that you are confusing the mid-July meeting with the people who were present at the early September meeting. Do you think you may be mistaken about that one, sir?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I am mistaken. I'm very sure that I went there with General Staff members for the meeting in mid-July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Very well. Certainly, it is agreed by Mr. Brahimaj that you came back to Jabllanice with transportation provided by Ramush Haradinaj in order to meet up with Lahi Brahimaj, who had an order from the General Staff that you should both proceed to Rahovec. That is agreed. And that would have been at around the time of the major Serb offensive that began approximately 18th to 19th of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. From Dukagjin, from Gllogjan I went to Jablanica. Lahi was waiting for me there, and he conveyed the order of the General Staff to me, that we both needed to go to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I think it's fair to say that you met him at his house and left almost immediately from there to Rahovec?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at his house, that's where we met, and from there we went straight to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And now on the second occasion when you were in Jabllanice - let me just pause there. Am I right in saying there were only two occasions when you were in Jabllanice: one in the mid-July and one at the very beginning of September. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not sure the witness's evidence, so far at least, has been that he visited Jablanica at the time of the -- what I might call the FARK visit at the end of August/beginning of September, but rather that he visited Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you about the early September visit. Do you recall at any stage in earlier September being in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Jabllanice, too --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because that was the way we had to pass through to go to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Exactly. And on the way back, in fact, did you pass back through Jabllanice as well?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you visit the KLA headquarters in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we visited the command post in Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And at any time when you were in the KLA command post, were you aware of anybody being detained there? I mean detained against their will?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my presence there, I didn't learn anything. I didn't hear or see anyone being detained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Could you just describe for us what kind of a facility the KLA command post in Jabllanice was; in other words, approximately how many buildings, how many soldiers did you see? If you remember, sir, it's a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the command post was placed in a private home. It was actually the home of Lahi Brahimaj. For the second time I visited it, I don't remember -- it was in a private home, but as to the number of soldiers, I can't give you an estimate. But it was the command there, the unit that guarded the command post in positions, in kind of defence positions. As to how many they were, this I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: May I suggest, sir, that you may be mistaken in saying that it was the home of Lahi Brahimaj; in fact, the home -- you visited the home of his cousin Ibrahim Brahimaj. Do you think that may be the correct picture, in fact?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked about July. From what I know, I visited the command post, which was placed in Lahi Brahimaj's home. During the second visit, I can't tell you whose house it was; I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Very well. How much time did you spend actually in the command post in July?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July, the first day we arrived there, we held a meeting between the General Staff and the zone commander. I visited the units there until the evening. Then in the evening, I continued my way to Gllogjan, so I would say a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So when you say you visited the units there, what do you mean by the units? Was there a sort of barracks place there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go to the barracks, there wasn't one. I went to the front line where the soldiers had taken up positions of defence. This is what I visited.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Very well. Just one minor matter in relation to Jabllanice. You had mentioned the name Driton Zeneli as having been, to your recollection, commander at Jabllanice at one point. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, because together with him, we visited some of the front line positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I want to suggest to you, sir, that he was indeed commander for a brief period between the Serb offensives of August and September of 1998 and, in fact, that he was killed in the front line in his position as commander of Jabllanice in the Serb offensive in September of 1998. Does that accord with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember when he was killed, but I was testifying about my visit to the front line, during which he was present, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And do you think that that would have been in the period in September, beginning of September?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall accurately. I already stated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That's very fair. Then I'd like to move to some more general questions about the role of the General Staff and its evolution. Prior to May 28th when you led the group that came into Kosovo, most of the General Staff were located outside Kosovo; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I entered Kosova, on the 28th of May, with me were also some other members when we entered. As I said, Hashim Thaqi, Kadri Veseli, Adem Grabovci, some others who were in Tirana -- yes, a large number of them was in Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In fact, up until then, the only members of the General Staff who were consistently inside Kosovo were Rexhep Selimi, Sokol Bashota, and Lahi Brahimaj. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who were inside, but it was later on that I learned that it was Rexhep Selimi and Sokol Bashota who stayed in Kosova during the time you are putting it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You are aware, I think, that Lahi Brahimaj was also somebody who had not left Kosovo, but he had stayed in the country the entire time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about him, what he did before. I already explained to you when I met him for the first time; from that moment onwards, I had contacts with him, and I do know that he didn't leave Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Right. Does it come to this, that before the meeting of the 23rd of June that Mr. Emmerson took you to yesterday, the minutes of that meeting in the Dukagjin Zone on the 23rd of June, it would appear that up until that date there was no unified command of the Dukagjin area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it was like before, but I was informed that there wasn't a general unified command --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That was --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- but I wasn't there, as I told you before that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was that also a similar situation to that going on in Drenica, there wasn't a unified command structure in Drenice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Drenice -- in Drenice the efforts had already started to unify the command and to ensure a better structuring of the army and the command, but I don't know about the Dukagjin Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And those were the two zones that were best organised; they were the most active zones at least, Dukagjin and Drenica, up until that point when you and your comrades entered Kosovo on the 28th of May?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already stated in my November statement, I said that both zones were more active in this period until we entered Kosova -- that is, during summer. And they had better -- they were better organised, were more active compared to other zones which developed later than them. Like, for example, Pashtrik Zone, Llap, Shala, Nerodime, Karadak Zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Exactly. The point is that up until the end of May, there was no real attempt to pull everything together and that was your mission when you, Hashim Thaqi, and your other comrades entered Kosova at the end of May; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what efforts were made because I cannot testify to a period I was not there, and I don't know what was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, but you were in the General Staff or working, at least, with General Staff members outside the country. What did you understand the reason to be for going into the country? Wasn't it so that you could organise things that had so far not been sufficiently organised and that could only be done from within the country?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My aim was to help them in organisation and improvement of the structure of the KLA. That was my task and that was a task of every officer or superior man in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And as Mr. Emmerson -- as you agreed with him yesterday, you were the only professional soldier in the entire group at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the group with which I entered Kosova, I wasn't the only professional, because there was Agim Cela, who was also a former JNA army officer; Agashi, also he was a former army officer; Kasapi also another one; Mahir Hasani also a former officer of the JNA and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I put my question too broadly. But you were the only member -- the only person who was going to go on to the General Staff as a professional soldier and help to reorganise the General Staff and the entire structure of the KLA. That was your primary function, wasn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task wasn't properly -- exactly defined when I was going to Kosova. That happened when I went to the General Staff, which was in Likofc. It was there that we were given the tasks and the responsibilities. It was there that I was appointed to work in the operational department, and Agim Cela, also along with me. But the others didn't have that kind of preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Right. Organising the General Staff at headquarters was a major task, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a major task, but the task applied also to the units below the general command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Exactly. For instance, you as a professional soldier -- you would differentiate between a command officer and a staff officer; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what respect do you mean I would differentiate between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That they have different areas of responsibilities. They perform different functions within a military structure?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they performed different tasks; that is, a commander has different tasks from a General Staff member.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And if you're a commander of a zone, that isn't a part-time job, is it? You can't be part-time commander, part-time staff officer on the General Staff? Sorry, let me rephrase that. You can't be part-time zone commander and part-time General Staff officer, can you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I haven't got any objection to these questions at all, but I think it would be -- in fact essential that you -- we know if the witness is speaking about theoretical situations or matters in a highly organised army or whether he's talking about the situation that applied in the situation he found himself in 1998. It's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think that's a perfectly reasonable proposal, and I intended to go in that direction with the witness in any event. So can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You rather explore what he knows about the situation at the time, rather than whether something is possible or not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I was approaching it from the standpoint of the fact that you as a professional soldier would organise things in one way. When you arrived, however, in the end of May/beginning of June 1998, did you find that people had organised themselves in a way that you approved of?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that the organisation -- their organisation wasn't the proper one in terms of military organisation or military formations in order to wage the war, as was the purpose or the goal of the KLA at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, we have heard, to be quite specific about this, you were taken yesterday by Mr. Emmerson to the document in which Lahi Brahimaj was appointed as deputy commander of the Dukagjin Zone. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: At that time, of course, Lahi Brahimaj was a serving member of the General Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the time when I was informed of the situation, when I was given the task of director, I saw Lahi, and he was introduced to me as director of the finance department in the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: All right. At the time you were given your responsibilities, he was already there serving as director of finances; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, this is what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You didn't know how long he'd been in that position, but he was certainly already in that position when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know when exactly he was given that responsibility, but I found him there when I went to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And to you, as a military man, it was a nonsense to suggest that Lahi Brahimaj could at the same time be director of finances on the General Staff and deputy commander of the Dukagjin Zone. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the military aspect, you are right, it doesn't make sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And as far as you're aware, he never actually functioned as a deputy commander in the Dukagjin Zone, did he?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the time prior to my arrival, I don't know what duty he had, whether he was deputy commander. I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm talking about the period between the 23rd of June, 1998, when we saw that order yesterday in which he was elected to that function. You were already there in Kosovo, weren't you, by the 23rd of June?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Kosova, but I don't know whether he was in that task or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You never -- you were never aware of him saying, Bislim, sorry, I've got to go to Jablanica tomorrow because I'm deputy commander of the zone. There was never any conversation of that sort took place with you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, no, and it was very short period since I got over my duty and went to the Dukagjini Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Right. I'd like to ask you a little about conditions in Drenica in which you in -- that's the General Staff had to operate. First of all, when you entered Kosovo on the 28th of May leading a group of some 80 men, it took you about a week to get to Likofc; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one week comprises my entry to Kosova, and my arrival in Drenica and Likofc.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: While I'm asking the next couple of questions, if we could have Defence Exhibit D300-0003 on the screens, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has it -- has it been assigned an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: To my knowledge, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, that would be ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So it's document -- document number, I should have said, not exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number D37, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. While we're waiting, this is a map of Drenica zone. Oh, there it is. I'll be coming to that in a moment with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you were on your way from Albania to Likofc, why did it take you so long?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have explained in my statements, when we entered Kosova on the 28th of May from Damjan, we went to Reskoc village of Rahovec commune. We stayed there for three or four days, I'm not sure, but then we went on towards Drenice. So it took us about a week until we arrived in Drenice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And on the way, were you dropping off men and munitions and rifles as you passed through?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived in Drenoc, yes, we dropped off some munitions. It was kind of military depot there because each of us had, apart from its personal arms, an extra set of weapons in order to be able to arm other members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when you arrived in Likofc, did you go to the house of a person who was known by the nickname of Raketi or Rocket?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember his house. I visited it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I think you had some five or six of your group still with you when you arrived at that house, including, of course, Hashim Thaqi, who was related to Raketi?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was that house in Likofc one of the safe houses, if I can use that term, that were periodically used by members of the General Staff to spend the night as they were going about their duties?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you have on the screen in front of you, sir, the map of Drenica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, part of Drenice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, part of Drenica, yes, indeed. And we can see in -- towards the north-east -- sorry, north-west - I always have this problem - north-west of -- corner of the map, Likofc is shown with an orange spot. Do you see that? It's now up at the top of your screen on the left?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I should explain for all present that the -- this is a map from the Limaj case, hence it's -- centres on Llapushnik. That's the only reason that we see the marking in the centre. It's not relevant for the purposes of this case, I just thought it would be helpful for everyone to get a little bit of an orientation of Drenica since we haven't previously looked at the area at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: May I just ask you, on your way to Likofc, did you pass through Jablanica? Was that one of your stopping-off points?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you arrived at Raketi's house in Likofc, do you remember that Lahi Brahimaj was, in fact, there when you came?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So your first recollection of meeting him was when you were working together in the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I remember, yes. When I was given the task of director of the operational department.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And where physically was that? Is it somewhere that you can see on the map now?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Berisha Mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, we can see with a red triangle the word "Berisha"; that is the village of Berisha. Can you describe for us where the Berisha Mountains are in relation to the village of Berisha?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Berisha Mountains include this part from the road that goes to Prishtine-Peje and includes all this area: Berisha, Klecke, up to the road in the direction of Prishtine-Prizren. This is the territory that we refer to as the Berisha Mountains; whereas, Berishe village is a village situated in the Berisha Mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, was the General Staff -- and again, I think we -- Mr. Emmerson asked you some questions about this yesterday. This term is -- is potentially quite misleading. At times, you refer to it as the central staff. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You think in my testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, I'm actually thinking back to your testimony in the Limaj case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If anybody wishes to follow it in the transcript, it's page 600 -- 6822.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If I could just read briefly from that. You said in answer to a question from counsel for Mr. Limaj, you said: "A traditional army organised in the tradition" -- I'm sorry. Let me put the question first: "Can you just describe mainly what the differences were between a regular, traditional army and its organisation, and what you found with the KLA in Kosovo?" Your answer: "A traditional army organised in a traditional way, its organisation begins with professional training of leaders from lower ranks, going up to higher ranks, and the soldiers also in those respective units are prepared starting from squads and going up to the level of brigade. An army which has a command with all professional military characteristics required for a traditional army has trained and schooled people militarily. However, the KLA was an army based on self-organisation. At that time, it had the central staff, as it was called at that time. It was a small staff, not professional one, not prepared for proper command." Now, do you recall making that statement in the Limaj case?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Can you explain, sir, what you mean by a central staff as being -- as differentiated from a proper one?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before the witness answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do apologise. An urgent matter has come up that I need to attend to urgently. Would Your Honour excuse me for just a few moments?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No disrespect intended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please -- would you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No need to repeat the question because I heard it. It is true that there was a central staff earlier. I don't know when it was formed. This was before I arrived and learned about the KLA. So the wording used at the time was the central staff, and then it changed into General Staff with the development of the staff itself, and that's why there is this formulation of this term used in the Limaj trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was it as a result of the re-organisation -- the restructuring that you helped to propose that it changed from central staff to General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a need, yes, to change at the time, and it was also my initiative. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: This passage of evidence may lead to some confusion, I suspect. The witness said: "It was true there was a central staff earlier, I don't know when it was formed." And then he said: "This was before I arrived and learned about the KLA." So it's not clear to me as to whether he's referring to the terminology "central staff" before he went into Kosovo or before he went into Albania or before he left wherever he was living to go to Albania.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm happy to explore that. MR. DI FAZIO: I think we need to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, I'm looking at the clock and despite the assurances that the Chamber has received that we would finish during the first session, Mr. Harvey, how much time -- I'm not blaming you, you're usually not consuming too much time. But at the same time, Mr. Emmerson said he arranged with all of you to stay within the limits, but that he could have half an hour more. Then, of course, the Chamber expects nothing else than that this would be effective. And again, I'm not blaming you, but time pressure is building up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I would think probably no more than ten minutes, maybe less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I then suggest that we do not take the break now, as usually, that you finish and you're encouraged to see whether seven or eight minutes would do. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, could you just perhaps, please, clarify for us your last answer. You referred to when you first learned about the central staff. You said that: "This was before I arrived and learned about the KLA." Before you arrived where, sir?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will explain. Before I entered Kosova and joined the KLA, and when I entered Kosovo for some time it was still called the central staff. When I mentioned the term earlier, I was referring to 1995 and 1996 when the KLA existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was the term "central staff" used to differentiate those who stayed in the centre, those who stayed inside Kosovo from those outside Kosovo? Was that perhaps the reason for the different nomenclature?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term was used as central staff, even outside Kosovo, but I heard of it even when I was in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Coming back then, sir, to the re-organisation, the restructuring of the General Staff, that took place at the end of July/beginning of August or it began, should I say?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I couldn't say that the re-organisation started then, because I joined the General Staff in July, but the re-organisation and the completion started later. When I became Chief of Staff, that's when proper organisation started and expansion as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That wasn't until November of 1998, if I recall correctly?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Just going back to our map for a moment, you've indicated I think that the General Staff met at a number of locations. I think you've mentioned Klecke. Divjak, is that another place where the staff met?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did meet in Divjak, especially from November onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Berisha as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And Novo Sello?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Novo Sello.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So, was there -- it sounds from that as if there was never one particular house or location where you would routinely meet?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're talking about the period from June to November, the staff moved a lot, changed a lot of places, because of security considerations, not only in the Berisha Mountains but also in other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And during that period - and I'm talking specifically the beginning of June to the end of September - did you see Lahi Brahimaj on a regular basis; and if so, what would you mean by "regular"? Weekly? Daily? Monthly?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, speaking about the period from July to September, I've -- I met Lahi a couple of times. But, as I said, I was always on the move. I went to areas where fighting was occurring. I can't say that I saw him every day or every week, but maybe -- maybe once a week or once a month. I can't tell you how often we met each other. It's -- the dynamics of the operations and the fightings was so intense that I had to move and help the zone commanders to organise their defence. So I am not sure how often I met him, once a week or once a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And as far as meetings of the General Staff were concerned, was it a question of one or two people meeting from time to time as and when they could, or was there a regular routine that the first Monday of every month everybody had to meet together in one particular place?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, because of the dynamics of the fightings and so on, we could not meet every week. It was when we had the opportunity to meet together with the General Staff to exchange ideas and to take decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I've no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Zyrapi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. Mr. Zyrapi, we'll have a break, and I'll first ask Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom because I'd like to raise one other matter briefly. Have the parties received, either electronically or in hard copy, the list prepared by the registrar where numbers are assigned to, may I say, the two binders --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- with a total of 140 documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask Madam Registrar, what exactly is the basis for the list? Have you used the material given to you by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the basis for it. Yes. Then could I ask the parties -- perhaps look at it and see whether we have confusion again. Mr. Di Fazio, if you would look at tab 138, that's the third from the bottom on the list of Madam Registrar. Could you please, since she worked on the basis of your information, that now is P259, isn't it? Do I identify U0001869, or do I find another document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the registry had some difficulties, and for that reason the document you provided to us -- to us at least in the binder which was U0014586, at least the English translation, and has now been replaced by U0001869. And that's the document Mr. Emmerson used. So therefore we see already shifting from one document -- luckily, the documents are almost the same. It's mainly the handwriting on the document that's different. MR. DI FAZIO: Sometimes with these exhibits, if Your Honours please, you have the same document that appears but it's identical but with annotations, a number might be added or it might have been signed by someone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, if we have numbers on lists, of course now it has been changed. I do understand for good reasons, but, of course, the Chamber is not informed about it. We see in 138, we see a document which is not exactly the same as we find under tab 11, as used by Mr. Emmerson. Now, again here it's not dramatic because the content -- the typed content is the same. Nevertheless, it could easily create confusion. So therefore, now we understand that what we find under tab 138 is not the document which has been assigned a number P259, and that P259 is rather the document Mr. Emmerson used under tab 11. Of course, the Chamber would like to hear soon from the parties where there are problems in relation to admission, and since we have now numbers marked for identification, I think it's easier to work on the basis of the list provided to us by Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. We've prepared a schedule which we're in a position to provide to Mr. Di Fazio over the break. He may not be in a position to assimilate it immediately. Essentially, the principles upon which objection is taken are pretty plain. It's where the witness has been unable to identify a document or unable to identify a signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. We will then hear from you at a later stage, and you'll further prepare for a efficient discussion on admission of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just indicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- there may be a brief procedural matter to deal with immediately before the evidence of the next witness and pertaining to it. It will be short. I'll try to resolve it with Mr. Kearney in the break, but I'm just giving Your Honours an indication that there may be a very short procedural matter to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll then have a break until quarter past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I just want to ask you some questions arising from your testimony this morning. You -- towards the end of your testimony and during the cross-examination of Mr. Harvey, you described dropping off some munitions after you crossed the border into Kosovo, and that you dropped them off at a kind of military depot. What precisely was this military depot?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we entered Kosovo in May, we went to the village of Drenoc, in the municipality of Rahovec. We stayed there for a couple of days. There was a small depot there where we left the weapons, the extra weapons, that each of us had. And then those guns or those weapons were sent to the areas where they were needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. That's precisely what I wanted to know. And do you know who was making the decision to send those guns to those areas, those various areas?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The General Staff decided where the weapons would go on the basis of the requests they had from different zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And can you tell us if they -- the areas -- these various areas, were they located at different part -- different places all over Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decisions were made about the zones that existed, such as Drenica and part of the Pashtrik Zone. That's what I remember from the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You also said today, and you were talking about Dukagjini Zone at least, that both zones, one of the zones that you were talking about - I'm sorry, I apologise, I can't remember the other one, I think it might have been Drenica, but certainly Dukagjini was one of them. You said "both zones were more active prior to the 28th of May." What did you mean by "more active"?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: By "more active," I meant that there was fighting going on in the area, so there were units that operated in those zones. So by "active," I mean militarily active, because also the attacks were more intense in those areas as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned to Mr. Harvey in the course of his cross-examination, that in July you went to Jablanica, and there you had a meeting with the zone commander and the General Staff but you didn't give us a name. I just want to tie that up. Which -- who are you talking about when you say you had a meeting with the zone commander? Who -- which individual was that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The zone commander was Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
